narrative:
The model estimates a 54% chance that you will leave your job, which is just over the threshold for predicting departure. As a result, the organization has decided to deny your promotion.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile. First, your total years of experience across all jobs (1-5 years) was the strongest influence, pulling the prediction toward staying rather than leaving. This is actually quite common among employees the model expects to remain with their employer. Second, the fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the most important factor pushing the prediction toward leaving. Having external opportunities often signals that an employee is considering or likely to move on. Third, working in the "other" sector (rather than medical or education) also nudged the outcome toward leaving, though to a lesser degree.

Taken together, your relatively short overall experience helps explain why the system sees some reason for you to stay, but the presence of outside job offers outweighs that and tips the balance toward expecting you to depart.

The organization should discuss with you what would make you want to stay long-term, while you may want to reflect on whether those external opportunities better match your goals. Addressing job satisfaction and growth opportunities could help retain talented employees like you in the future. (218 words)
